name: 3d-conditional-gan-training
description: Use when the goal is volumetric (256x256x256) cross-modality neuroimage synthesis — e.g., predicting PET, fractional anisotropy, or mean diffusivity maps from T1w/FLAIR MRI — and stable 3D GAN training plus baseline comparison on NRMSE/PSNR/SSIM is required.

name: 3d-scan-intensity-visualization
description: Use when the input is a raw MS run (e.g. a Thermo Orbitrap Q Exactive acquisition from ProteomeXchange) and the goal is exploratory plotting of scan-level peak data — heat maps, 3D scan maps, or isotopic-envelope zooms — rather than identification or quantification.

name: 3d-self-attention-module-implementation
description: Use when building or verifying the self-attention blocks of a 3D conditional GAN for volumetric neuroimage synthesis (e.g., PET/FA/MD prediction from T1w and FLAIR MRI) in TensorFlow.

name: adc-event-readout-handoff-logic
description: Use when integrating a Pulseq-defined CEST preparation block into an existing vendor readout (e.g., 3D snapshot GRE or native EPI) and you need a clean mechanism to transfer execution from the interpreter to the native readout.

name: admm-constrained-optimization-execution
description: Use when a time-optimal MRI gradient waveform must be generated on-the-fly from a flexible set of input constraints (moments, eddy currents, PNS, b-value, duty cycle) using GrOpt's ADMM solver.

name: admm-solver-configuration
description: Use when you need to solve a constrained MRI gradient waveform design problem — e.g. gmax, smax, gradient moment nulling, eddy current or PNS constraints — via GrOpt's ADMM solver and need correct stopping, tolerance, and warm-start configuration.

name: adni-neuroimaging-data-handling
description: Use when raw ADNI-3 MRI/PET downloads must be turned into analysis-ready 256x256x256 training/testing volumes for cross-modality synthesis (e.g., MRI-to-PET or MRI-to-FA/MD) with quality metrics such as NRMSE, peak SNR, and SSIM.
tools: LONI pipeline (Laboratory of Neuro Imaging pipeline)

name: adversarial-training-stabilization-techniques
description: Use when training a 3D conditional GAN for cross-modality image synthesis (e.g. T1w+FLAIR MRI to amyloid PET) shows unstable or non-converging adversarial optimization, and you need spectral normalization/feature-matching stabilization.

name: amino-acid-frequency-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a MUSCLE multiple sequence alignment of protein variants and need per-position absolute and relative amino acid occurrence tables, or a consensus sequence with user-defined conservation thresholding.

name: ant-colony-optimization-graph-search
description: Use when peptide identification from tandem mass spectrometry data must match theoretical database peptide sequences against a combinatorial spectrum graph, especially with mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications, large databases, or low-quality spectra.

name: aromaticity-index-computation
description: Use when you have FT-ICR MS molecular formula lists (element composition with C/H/O/N/P/S) and need aromaticity classification or DBE-based traits for dissolved organic matter molecules.

name: asa-benchmark-validation-against-reference
description: Use when you have reimplemented or modified a solvent-exposure calculation (water molecules in possible contact per residue) and need to prove numerical correctness against published reference ASA values.

name: auc-based-signature-performance-thresholding
description: Use when you have a muSignAl output table of candidate signatures (e.g. sign_cvd2.xlsx) with per-signature AUC values and need to select the high-performing subset above a specified AUC threshold such as 0.95.

name: auc-model-evaluation
description: Use when repeated subsample models (e.g. Elastic Net glmnet fits) must be scored for predictive performance and filtered on AUC > 0.5 before downstream feature selection.

name: auc-threshold-signature-filtering
description: Use when a signature-search output (e.g. muSignAl's sign_cvd2.xlsx) lists many feature panels with performance scores and you must retain only those above a defined AUC threshold and profile feature recurrence.

name: b-factor-profile-normalization
description: Use when you have X-ray protein structures in PDB format (ATOMIC ATOM records with Cα B-factors) and need normalized B'-factor/ΔB' profiles or mobility-based (rigidification vs. flexibility gain) interpretation at ligand-binding sites.

name: benchmark-method-comparison
description: Use when a proposed classifier must be compared head-to-head with a published baseline on the same benchmark dataset and negative-sample segmentation, and mean AUC/Acc/Precision must be assembled into a comparison table.

name: betanti-null-model-computation
description: Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM molecular compositional data (e.g. MCD, TD, or TWCD molecular dendrograms) must be tested for deterministic versus stochastic assembly via betaNTI null modeling.

name: bidirectional-lstm-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw protein sequences in FASTA format must be converted into dense numerical embeddings for a machine-learning classifier (e.g. identifying plant R proteins with LGBM), and pretrained deep representation learning models are available.

name: binary-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when two or more binary classifier variants (e.g., a stacked ensemble vs. its base learners) must be compared on the same test set, especially under class imbalance where AUPRC and recall at probability thresholds matter more than accuracy.

name: binary-classifier-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier's predictions on held-out test samples (e.g., the 92-sample plant R protein independent test) must be scored with accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC and compared to published values.

name: biomarker-panel-prioritization
description: Use when a muSignAl run yields many candidate biomarker signatures (e.g. 158 panels from Olink CVD-II in sign_cvd2.xlsx) and you must rank or threshold them by AUC to shortlist panels worth developing.

name: biomarker-signature-thresholding
description: Use when building an omic biomarker signature from a feature/sample matrix and you need a stability-based cutoff (feature frequency across resampled models) rather than a single-model coefficient ranking.

name: bloch-mcconnell-simulation
description: Use when a CEST protocol is defined as a Pulseq .seq file and you need simulated Z-spectra to test or optimize the saturation preparation period in silico, or to validate simulations against measured Z-spectra.

name: boosted-tree-classifier-training
description: Use when a set of extracted/embedded feature vectors must be fed to boosted-tree or ensemble classifiers and compared (e.g. CatBoost vs XGBoost vs RF vs GBDT) with CV-based metrics such as Acc, Sp, Sn, MCC and AUC.

name: bootstrap-subsampling-replicate-analysis
description: Use when comparing co-occurrence network statistics between known-formula (KK) and dark-matter-inclusive (DK) networks from DOM molecular formula tables, since network metrics like degree centrality depend on node count and subsampling removes that confound.

name: boxplot-visualization-across-cancer-types
description: Use when you need to rank or compare the expression abundance of a single gene (e.g., TP53 mRNA) across many cancer types from a pancancer cell line expression matrix, or when reproducing IMOPAC-style Cancer Types Summary plots.

name: brain-area-rmse-loss-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reproducing the SC-GAN generator objective (adversarial + L1 + feature matching + brain-area RMSE terms) and the B-rmse term must be computed on the brain mask only.

name: brain-tissue-regional-error-mapping
description: Use when a synthesized 3D neuroimaging volume (e.g., FA, MD, or PET predicted from T1w and FLAIR) must be evaluated for tissue-specific accuracy beyond a single whole-brain error scalar.

name: brno-nomenclature-ptm-annotation
description: Use when Mascot .xml results of histone peptide searches (phosphorylation S/T/Y, acetylation K, mono-/di-methylation K/R, trimethylation K) need standardized Brno-style PTM labels before abundance quantification.

name: brno-nomenclature-ptm-string-parsing
description: Use when Mascot .xml/.csv output from middle-down histone MS/MS runs must be converted to standardized PTM strings and parsed to enumerate combinatorial marks (e.g. K4me3K14ac, H3K27me3K36me3) per peptide.

name: calibration-curve-linear-regression
description: Use when you have replicate-grouped dilution-series intensities for one or more peptides (e.g. transition-level data for WTVFQK/MFAP4) and must determine the linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) and judge calibration fit quality beyond R-squared alone.

name: calibration-curve-visualization
description: Use when you have fitted calibration models (weighted/unweighted) and a determined linear range from a targeted mass-spectrometry concentration or dilution series and need to assess calibration accuracy visually.

name: calibration-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw targeted-MS calibration data from a concentration or dilution series (e.g. msqc1 xlsx files such as GGPFSDSYR_QExactive_y5.xlsx) must be loaded and cleaned before determining dynamic linear ranges and quantification limits.

name: calibration-level-iterative-trimming
description: Use when a concentration–response calibration table (replicate measurements per level, e.g. from SRM/MRM/PRM assays) shows non-linearity at the extremes — e.g. reduced product ion intensities at high analyte concentrations — and Cl/Ch limits of quantification must be computed.

name: calibration-model-summary-reporting
description: Use when a targeted proteomics (SRM/MRM or PRM) calibration experiment with concentration/dilution series data needs linear-range determination, precision/trueness result tables, and calibration-curve plus response-factor figures.

name: cancer-cell-line-data-processing
description: Use when a pancancer expression matrix from cell line models (e.g., DepMap/GDSC/NCI60) must be joined to cancer-type metadata and summarized per cancer type for a specific gene such as TP53.

name: cbow-word-embedding-feature-generation
description: Use when raw GPCR amino-acid sequences must be converted into dense numerical feature vectors (word embeddings) for downstream classification, e.g. feeding CatBoost/XGBoost in a GPCR identification task.

name: cbp60-family-sequence-curation
description: Use when building a reference database of all homologs of a gene family (e.g. CBP60) across phylogenetically diverse published plant genomes and you need verified counts of unique genes, transcripts, and proteins.

name: central-difference-derivative-computation
description: Use when normalized, smoothed DSF melting curves are available and a per-well first-derivative curve is needed to locate the derivative peak corresponding to the melting temperature (Tm).

name: cest-pool-configuration
description: Use when simulating CEST Z-spectra from pulseq .seq-files and a pool configuration (CEST pools, semi-solid MTC pool, line shape) must be specified in a yaml config before running the Bloch-McConnell simulation.

name: cest-z-spectral-processing
description: Use when raw multislice/multisite CEST-MRF or CEST images need to be converted into quantitative maps (fMT, kMT, fAmide, kAmide) with B0/B1 correction and dictionary-based signal matching.

name: chimeric-transcript-annotation
description: Use when a cell line's RNA-seq fusion calls (STAR-Fusion output with SpliceType, LargeAnchorSupport, FFPM columns) must be filtered to biologically credible fusions and visualized as a Circos plot.

name: chromatographic-retention-time-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when replicate LC-MS/MS runs of histone tail separations are available and the goal is to quantify run-to-run retention-time variation per histone tail class (H3, H4, H2A) against explicit minute-level acceptance thresholds.

name: class-imbalance-weighted-training
description: Use when training binary classifiers on datasets with strong positive/negative label imbalance (e.g., rare phosphorylation sites in plants) where recall on the minority class is the priority and standard training under-predicts positives.

name: class-imbalanced-protein-dataset-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking protein sequence classifiers on a dataset with unequal positive/negative counts (e.g., 1:2 ratio like 152 R proteins vs 304 non-R), where accuracy alone can mask weak minority-class recall and F1/AUC must be reported alongside it.

name: classification-metrics-computation
description: Use when two or more binary protein classifiers (e.g., prPred-DRLF vs prPred vs HMMER) must be compared on the same 92-sequence independent test set using ACC, F1-score, AUC, and recall deltas.

name: classification-threshold-beta-sweep
description: Use when comparing phosphosite classifiers whose AUROC or AUPRC alone masks recall differences, and the analysis goal is to quantify at what recall-vs-precision weighting (beta) one classifier overtakes another.

name: classifier-performance-curve-visualization
description: Use when comparing classifiers whose AUPRC/AUROC are similar but whose recall priorities differ, and you need to identify at which beta (recall-weighting) one classifier's F-beta surpasses another.

name: classifier-prediction-count-comparison
description: Use when a classifier's predicted false positives need to be relabeled as inferred positives via sequence alignment against experimentally derived phosphosites, and the improvement must be quantified per classifier.

name: classifier-probability-score-extraction
description: Use when a trained per-site classifier must produce residue-level predicted probability scores (per-Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphosite csv files) as input for recall, AUPRC, or F-beta benchmarking against other methods.

name: cnv-alteration-frequency-analysis
description: Use when a task asks for pancancer CNV alteration frequency of a specific gene across cancer types in patient-derived cancer cell lines, or to replicate the IMOPAC 'Cancer Types Summary' CNV module from DepMap CNV data.

name: coarse-to-fine-warm-start-optimization
description: Use when a time-optimal MRI gradient waveform duration T must be found on-the-fly (within 1-40 ms) and a naive single-threaded sequential scan over durations T = dt*N is too slow.

name: colabfold-alphafold2-structure-inference
description: Use when you have amino acid sequences for a protein family and need predicted 3D structures plus confidence metrics (pLDDT, PAE, pTM) without running full AlphaFold2 locally.

name: collision-energy-calibration
description: Use when search-engine results and spectra (raw/mzml/d/hdf) are available and you need the per-file optimal NCE for Prosit/Koina spectral predictions, e.g. before spectral library generation or rescoring.

name: comet-database-searching
description: Use when raw immunopeptidomics (MHC-bound peptide) MS/MS data has been converted to MGF and you need PSM-level peptide-spectrum matches against a target-decoy protein database for downstream FDR filtering, rescoring, or validation.

name: common-spectra-interface-reconstruction
description: Use when the input is a text-based peak list file (DTA, MGF, MS2, PKL, mzXML, mzData, mzML) that must be converted into structured per-spectrum records, or when mzIdentML spectrum references must be resolved against external peak list files.

name: computational-complexity-scaling-analysis
description: Decision support for determining whether a numerical optimization routine (e.g., GrOpt ADMM gradient waveform design) is fast enough for on-the-fly use, and for quantifying how constraint sets change its asymptotic compute-time scaling with input size N.

name: compute-time-tabulation-across-discretization
description: Use when you need to quantify how a chosen gradient waveform discretization N affects the minimum TE (or compute feasibility) of an optimized diffusion waveform, e.g. to justify a raster-time/point-count choice before production waveform design.

name: consecutive-threshold-interval-selection
description: Use when replicate intensity measurements are grouped by concentration level and a contiguous interval of levels passing a CV threshold (MeasCV <= TMeasCV) must be extracted, e.g. to define the lower bound of a linear range for SRM/MRM or PRM calibration data.

name: consensus-sequence-construction
description: Use when you have a MUSCLE multiple sequence alignment of variant sequences (or BLAST-retrieved homologs with an applied identity cutoff) and need a per-position consensus protein sequence to drive conservation scoring or PDB structure lookup.

name: conservation-metric-superimposition-on-3d-structure
description: Use when you have a multiple sequence alignment (or SNP matrix) with per-position conservation/entropy or SNP frequency/type values and a PDB structure on which to visualize them.

name: coulombic-electrostatic-modeling
description: Use when atomic coordinates (PDB/mmCIF) must be converted into backbone hydrogen-bond assignments, e.g. to derive DSSP-style secondary structure, base-pair maps, or per-pair bond energies from N, C, O, CA coordinates.

name: cpp-sequence-interpreter-implementation
description: Use when a pulseq-file-defined CEST preparation block must be executed on a vendor scanner inside an established readout sequence without modifying that readout or its reconstruction.

name: cross-condition-ptm-crosstalk-comparison
description: Use when you have Mascot-searched middle-down/top-down histone MS/MS data (Histone Coder result file + Mascot .csv) and need to compare co-detection fractions of specific PTM pairs between two or more biological conditions.

name: cross-format-parser-conformance-testing
description: Use when validating that peak list parsers across several MS file formats (DTA, MS2, MGF, PKL, mzXML, mzData, mzML, PRIDE XML) return consistent spectra through one API, e.g. for mzIdentML external-spectra referencing.

name: cross-language-numerical-validation
description: Use when the same computational model exists in two languages (e.g., MATLAB and Python) and you must prove the implementations agree on identical inputs before trusting either output.

name: cross-method-quantification-agreement-analysis
description: Use when the same set of peptide groups (e.g. 22 H3 groups spanning 0-3 acetyl and 0-9 methyl PTM equivalents) has been quantified by two or more label-free approaches and you need per-group agreement against a reference quantification.

name: cross-model-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when several trained synthesis/generation models must be compared on identical test data with quantitative image-quality metrics to establish which architecture outperforms the baselines.

name: cross-model-compute-cost-tabulation
description: Use when multiple network variants (e.g., SC-GAN vs 2D/3D/attention conditional GANs) have been trained under the same regime and you must compare their wall-clock training burden per epoch and to plateau.

name: cross-search-engine-peptide-overlap-analysis
description: Use when multiple search engines (e.g., Comet, MS-GF+, X!Tandem, MaxQuant) have been run on the same immunopeptidomics datasets and you need to quantify peptide-level consensus versus single-engine-unique identifications, especially before and after Percolator-style rescoring.

name: cross-species-phosphosite-prediction-transfer
description: Use when you need genome-wide phosphosite probability scores for a species lacking its own trained model, and have a trained PhosBoost .pkl plus a proteome FASTA file.

name: cross-validated-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when a small labeled training set (e.g., 364 sequences) must be split across multiple classifier and feature-selection methods to identify the -performing combination before independent testing.

name: cross-validation-model-assessment
description: Use when a trained classifier (e.g., LGBM on BiLSTM/UniRep/TAPE-BERT feature subsets) must be validated before reporting performance, requiring both cross-validation and an independent test evaluation.

name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing GPCR identification methods (e.g., EMCBOW-GPCR vs. Liao's SVM-Prot 188D + SMOTE + RF) under a stated SMOTE-balancing protocol, so that per-fold Acc/AUC can be aggregated into a fair side-by-side metrics table.

name: cross-vendor-mri-pulse-sequence-comparison
description: Use when a diffusion or flow encoding protocol must run comparably on scanners from different vendors (e.g., GE and Siemens) and you need to prove waveform-level functional equivalence rather than just image-level similarity.

name: curve-segment-boundary-detection
description: Use when a normalized DSF melting curve must be partitioned before smoothing or downstream Tm analysis, and the denaturation region needs to be delimited by the curve's minimum and maximum fluorescence points.

name: curve-smoothing-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you have 96-well (or multi-well plate) DSF raw fluorescence melting curves and need to verify that a smoothing routine does not shift Tm values derived from the FDC maximum before adopting it for Tm analysis.

name: cv-parameter-extraction
description: Use when an mzIdentML file or downstream tool references an external mzData peak list file and you must extract spectrum IDs, cvParam metadata, and peak arrays into a structured record per spectrum.

name: cz-fragment-ion-series-interpretation
description: Use when Mascot database-search results (.xml) from ETD middle-down histone MS/MS must have PTM localizations confirmed by site-determining c/z ions before downstream quantification of combinatorial marks.

name: dark-matter-cooccurrence-network-construction
description: Use when an FT-ICR MS molecular formula table contains both characterized formulas and dark matter (unannotated peaks) and the goal is to quantify the effect of dark matter on DOM molecular interactions, e.g. comparing temperate vs. subtropical warming treatments.

name: de-novo-spectrum-graph-modeling
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists (m/z + intensity per fragment peak) must be converted into a structured spectrum-graph representation before matching theoretical peptide sequences from a database, as Popitam does for mutation/unexpected-PTM characterization.

name: delta-b-prime-binding-site-interpretation
description: Use when analyzing X-ray protein-ligand complex structures (e.g. PDB entries) to derive ligand-optimization hypotheses from binding-site mobility changes, such as building B'-factor-supported pharmacophore models.

name: dendrogram-mntd-diversity-calculation
description: Use when molecular compositional data from FT-ICR MS must be converted into a dendrogram of molecular relatedness so that MNTD-style functional diversity can be computed per assemblage across an experimental gradient.

name: depmap-rnaseq-fusion-data-processing
description: Use when a task needs to process DepMap Public 22Q1 RNA-seq fusion calls (STAR-Fusion format) for a specific cell line and produce a filtered, plot-ready fusion-gene-pair table or fusion Circos visualization.

name: derivative-curve-peak-identification
description: Use when raw multi-well DSF fluorescence melting curves (e.g. a 96-well plate) need Tm values and the FD method (Tm = temperature at max of the FDC) should be applied, including verification that smoothing preserves Tm.

name: desikan-killiany-atlas-parcellation
description: Use when regional SUVR quantification of amyloid PET (measured or GAN-synthesized, e.g. AV45) is needed over the 110 Desikan-Killiany subcortical and cortical regions, with a paired T1w image available for parcellation and masking.

name: deterministic-stochastic-process-classification
description: Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM compositional data and molecular dendrograms (e.g., MCD, TD, TWCD) are available and the goal is to classify pairwise assembly turnover as deterministic variable selection, homogeneous selection, or stochastic using betaNTI thresholds.

name: diamond-protein-sequence-alignment
description: Use when classification-only phosphosite predictions (e.g. PhosBoost S/T predictions) contain false positives that could be recovered as inferred positives by aligning 31-residue peptide windows against a curated plant phosphosite database such as qPTMplants.

name: differential-abundance-gene-list-matching
description: Use when you have a mass-matched peptide identification table and a list of gene names from an upstream differential-abundance step, and need to keep only peptides attributable to proteins of the tissue-of-interest signature (e.g., HSIL(+) cluster).

name: differential-abundance-significance-testing
description: Use when two isobarically-labeled conditions (e.g., TMT6plex SPS-MS3 glucose vs pyruvate) must be compared at the protein level, especially to test whether QC-score-based scan filtering shifts the set of significant proteins.

name: diffusion-b-value-encoding-design
description: Use when a diffusion protocol (e.g. b=1000 mm2/s, six-direction tensor encoding) needs a gradient waveform that meets Gmax/Smax hardware limits and moment nulling on a specific scanner, or when waveforms must be reproduced across GE and Siemens platforms.

name: diffusion-encoding-moment-nulling-configuration
description: Use when designing time-optimal diffusion-encoding gradient waveforms (e.g., b = 1000 mm2/s) with moment nulling or eddy-current nulling constraints and choosing N/dt so minimum TE is within ~1 ms of the shortest feasible TE.

name: diffusion-encoding-waveform-design
description: Use when a diffusion MRI sequence (e.g., spin-echo EPI DWI) needs a shortest feasible gradient waveform for a target b-value while honoring Gmax/Smax hardware limits, gradient moment compensation, or eddy-current nulling.

name: diffusion-metric-map-synthesis
description: Use when the task is predicting a 3D quantitative diffusion metric map (MD, FA) from structural MRI modalities such as T1w and FLAIR in high-resolution (256 x 256 x 256) volumes and comparing GAN-based synthesis quality.

name: diffusion-mri-superresolution
description: Use when low-resolution multidimensional diffusion MRI volumes (e.g., 41×46×28 MUDI images with 1344 diffusion directions) must be upsampled to a higher target grid (e.g., 82×92×56), or when comparing GAN-based superresolution against 3D Unet/3D cGAN baselines.

name: dimensionality-reduction-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a large pairwise similarity or distance matrix (e.g., TM-Align structural similarity scores) must be embedded in 2D for cluster visualization and a choice must be made between UMAP and t-SNE on speed and projection quality.

name: discrete-omic-group-comparison-testing
description: Use when comparing drug sensitivity (AUC/IC50) between two cell-line subgroups defined by a discrete molecular alteration (e.g., mutated vs wild-type status of a user-defined gene) in GDSC, DepMap, or NCI60 pharmacogenomic data.

name: dissolved-organic-matter-molecular-class-assignment
description: Use when you have a DOM FT-ICR MS molecular formula table (elemental compositions, e.g., CHO/CHON/CHOS) and need each molecule assigned to a molecular class and to labile/recalcitrant active/inactive reactivity–activity fractions.

name: distributed-peptide-sharing-across-protein-families
description: Use when Morpheus search-engine output maps peptides to multiple proteins within a protein family or isoform/proteoform group, and label-free quantification must attribute shared spectra across those members rather than discarding them.

name: disulfide-bond-detection-from-structures
description: Use when you have a PDB or mmCIF coordinate file (optionally gzipped) and need per-residue disulfide-bond annotations plus geometric features (bend, chirality) written to a structured table such as dssp_geometry_annotations.csv.

name: dom-assembly-process-quantification
description: Use when FT-ICR MS molecular compositional data of dissolved organic matter are available and the goal is to classify pairwise turnover between assemblages into deterministic (variable/homogeneous selection) versus stochastic assembly processes via betaNTI null modeling.

name: dom-dissimilarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have a sample-by-molecular-formula DOM table (presence/absence plus relative abundance) from FT-ICR MS and need chemical diversity/dissimilarity metrics or a test of whether DOM composition differs between sample groupings.

name: dom-microbe-bipartite-network-construction
description: Use when you have FT-ICR MS-derived DOM molecular intensity data paired with microbial abundance tables and need to quantify bipartite DOM-microbe associations and their network-level specialization under an experimental treatment (e.g., warming).

name: dom-molecular-trait-visualization
description: Use when FT-ICR MS molecular compositional tables with relative abundances sampled across treatments (e.g., six experimental warming temperature levels in temperate and subtropical regions) must be summarized into per-sample diversity indices and tested against the gradient.

name: dom-molecule-temperature-correlation
description: Use when FT-ICR MS DOM molecular compositional matrices are paired with per-sample temperature (or another environmental gradient) metadata and the goal is to quantify thermal responses at both the molecular (MER) and compositional (iCER) levels.

name: dom-relative-abundance-aggregation-by-class
description: Use when you have a DOM FT-ICR MS formula table (with elemental compositions enabling H/C and O/C molecular traits) and need molecular class assignment plus labile/recalcitrant active/inactive fraction classification with relative-abundance summaries.

name: double-bond-equivalent-estimation
description: Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM molecular formulae (with elemental compositions C, H, O, N, P, S) need per-molecule unsaturation descriptors — DBE, DBEO, DBEAI — as input to molecular-trait tables or chemical diversity analyses.

name: drug-omics-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you want to identify gene–drug associations from multiomics and drug sensitivity matrices of GDSC, DepMap, or NCI60 cell lines in IMOPAC, for a user-defined gene of interest.

name: dsf-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing DSF melting curves (e.g., from His-FGF10 thermal stability assays) to normalize, smooth, and extract Tm values from first derivative curves, including automated second-Tm recognition and unfolded/denatured classification.

name: dsf-first-derivative-curve-peak-detection
description: Use when classifying DSF melting curves via peaks in normalized, smoothed first derivative curves (FDCs): qualifying peaks must exceed 10% of the highest peak's width and height; flag no-Tm curves (>=4 peaks) and unfolded curves (declining MC).

name: dsf-fluorescence-data-processing
description: Use when normalized DSF melting curves contain fluorescence noise that would distort melting temperature (Tm) estimation, and a shape-preserving smoothing step is needed before Tm analysis.

name: dsf-melting-curve-processing
description: Use when raw DSF fluorescence-versus-temperature melting curves (e.g. a 96-well plate) must be normalized, smoothed, and converted to per-well Tm values, or when checking whether smoothing perturbs FD-method Tm values.

name: dsf-melting-curve-smoothing-comparison
description: Use when you have raw DSF melting curves plus SimpleDSFviewer-smoothed counterparts (e.g. His-FGF7 + 50 µM heparin exemplar) and must verify smoothing preserves MC shape via per-point difference analysis.

name: dsf-thermal-stability-analysis
description: Use when the input is DSF fluorescence melting-curve data (e.g. a 96-well exemplar plate ramp) and the goal is to compute normalized FD curves, extract per-well Tm values, or compare Tm from smoothed vs unsmoothed MCs.

name: dssp-strip-table-generation
description: Use when you need per-residue standardized secondary-structure assignments (helices, ladders, sheets, turns, bends, chirality, exposure) computed from protein coordinate files and rendered as linear strip tables.

name: dti-derived-quantitative-map-normalization
description: Use when quantitative DTI-derived targets (FA or MD maps) or input MR images are being prepared for training/testing the SC-GAN or baseline cGANs in the ADNI-3 FA/MD/PET synthesis tasks, where stable training requires intensities scaled between 0 and 1.

name: dynamic-linear-range-determination
description: Use when replicate concentration–response data from a targeted MS dilution series (e.g. SRM/MRM, PRM) must be reduced to a defensible linear range with LLOQ/ULOQ, instead of eyeballing response-factor plots.

name: ecological-null-model-interpretation
description: Use when FT-ICR MS-derived DOM compositional data and molecular trait dendrograms (e.g. MCD, TD, TWCD) are available and the goal is to classify pairwise turnover into variable selection, homogeneous selection, or stochastic processes via betaNTI.

name: eddy-current-nulling-constraint-configuration
description: Use when designing time-optimal MRI gradient waveforms (e.g., diffusion encoding in spin-echo EPI DWI) where eddy-current-induced image artifacts must be suppressed by nulling specific eddy-current time constants via GrOpt constraints.

name: elastic-net-feature-selection
description: Use when a tabular omics matrix (e.g. Olink proteomics samples x features in .xlsx) must be reduced to predictive biomarker signatures via Elastic Net, with FI >= 0.9 cutoff and pROC AUC-based model filtering.

name: elemental-composition-parsing
description: Use when you have a DOM molecular formula table (element counts C, H, O, N, P, S per molecule, e.g. from FT-ICR MS) and need per-molecule traits such as O/C, H/C, AImod, DBE, GFE, NOSC, or Ymet.

name: example-dataset-result-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce a published iDOM molGroup classification result on the bundled warming FT-ICR MS example dataset and verify class/fraction composition against reported figures.

name: extracted-ion-chromatogram-quantification
description: Use when relative abundances of histone N-terminal tail peptide groups (e.g. H3 species spanning 0-3 acetyl and 0-9 methyl PTM equivalents) must be quantified from LC-ESI-MS/MS runs and compared across technical replicates or against other quantification approaches.

name: f-beta-score-computation
description: Use when comparing classifiers on imbalanced phosphosite predictions and you need to know which method wins when recall is prioritized over precision (beta > 1), not just at F1 or AUPRC.

name: fa-map-synthesis-from-multimodal-mri
description: Use when the goal is to predict DTI-derived FA volumes from structural multimodal MRI (T1w + FLAIR) with a 3D GAN, and when quantitative image-quality metrics (NRMSE, PSNR, SSIM) against ground-truth FA are the expected output.

name: fasta-sequence-clustering
description: Use when a labeled protein dataset in FASTA format (e.g., plant R protein positives and negatives) must be deduplicated before feature extraction and classifier training.

name: fasta-sequence-handling
description: Use when raw protein sequences downloaded from UniProt must be turned into a homology-reduced benchmark dataset in FASTA format before classifier training or cross-validation (e.g., sequences sharing >= 80% identity need to be collapsed).

name: feature-ablation-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a rescoring or classification pipeline adds engineered features and you must decide which features drive the performance gain, by retraining the model with subsets removed and comparing peptide counts at a fixed FDR.

name: feature-importance-frequency-estimation
description: Use when building omic feature-selection pipelines on high-dimensional datasets where stability of selected biomarkers across resampled models, not a single model's coefficients, should define feature importance.

name: feature-importance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you need to enumerate multiple candidate biomarker signatures from a labeled omics dataset (e.g. proteomics matrix) without exploring all feature combinations, by ranking features with Elastic Net and applying an FI cutoff.

name: feature-matching-loss-implementation
description: Use when training a conditional GAN (e.g., SC-GAN for MRI/PET/DTI synthesis) and the generator loss must include a feature matching term alongside the cGAN adversarial loss, L1 loss, and brain-area RMSE loss to stabilize training.

name: feature-selection-matrix-handling
description: Use when a labeled protein feature matrix (e.g., 5505D fused BiLSTM+UniRep vectors for R vs non-R plant proteins) is too high-dimensional for direct classification and feature importance-based dimensionality reduction is needed.

name: feature-subset-selection
description: Use when input is protein sequences embedded into high-dimensional vectors (e.g., 3605D BiLSTM, 1900D UniRep, 768D TAPE-BERT, or 5505D fusions) and a compact discriminative subset must be selected before training a classifier.

name: feature-vector-concatenation-fusion
description: Use when multiple per-sequence embedding vectors (e.g. BiLSTM 3605D and UniRep 1900D from eFeature) must be merged into one fixed-width feature matrix before classifier training, with exact dimensionality checks.

name: firr-relative-quantification
description: Use when Mascot-identified MS/MS spectra contain two isobaric histone peptides sharing the same sequence but distinct PTM localizations, and each species needs a separate relative abundance from one composite spectrum.

name: five-fold-cross-validation-classifier-evaluation
description: Use when several candidate classifiers must be compared on the same precomputed feature matrix (e.g., Layer-1 DL features) and a defensible algorithm choice is needed, as in the EMCBOW-GPCR work.

name: fluorescence-curve-normalization
description: Use when you have smoothed, normalized DSF melting curves (MCs) sampled at a uniform temperature increment and need the first-derivative curve (FDC) whose peak marks each well's melting temperature.

name: fluorescence-melting-curve-quality-interpretation
description: Decision support for validating DSF melting-temperature calls across a multi-well plate: when per-well HMD and FD Tm values must be joined and discrepancy classes (averaged two-species Tm, not-calculable Tm) flagged before reporting results.

name: focal-loss-binary-classification-training
description: Use when a high-dimensional concatenated feature vector (e.g., 1011-D word-embedding + bag-of-words GPCR features) must be reduced via a trained DL module whose Layer-1 output is the final representation.

name: fragment-ion-intensity-scoring
description: Use when iTRAQ/TMT/TMTpro-labeled PSMs need interference QC scores computed per scan from b/y fragment ion intensity fractions in mzML data, to filter compressed reporter ion quantifications.

name: fragment-ion-mz-intensity-extraction
description: Use when you have an X!Tandem XML output file and need the underlying fragment-ion m/z and intensity values for each parsed spectrum, e.g. for downstream spectral inspection or identification detail tables.

name: fragment-spectrum-metadata-extraction
description: Use when you have X!Tandem XML result files and need to export detailed per-spectrum identification fields (peptide, E-value, hyperscore, protein accession, spectrum details) into a spreadsheet-openable format.

name: fticr-ms-compositional-data-filtering
description: Use when an FT-ICR MS molecule-by-sample compositional matrix contains low-prevalence molecules and downstream statistics (e.g., Spearman MER vs. temperature, iCER thermal response) require a prevalence-filtered abundance table.

name: fticr-ms-elemental-ratio-categorization
description: Use when an FT-ICR MS DOM peak/formula table (e.g., molecular formulae with elemental composition) needs categorical molecular class and reactivity–activity fraction assignment for compositional summarization.

name: fticr-ms-molecular-composition-analysis
description: Use when FT-ICR MS yields a samples-by-molecular-formula compositional table (presence/absence plus relative abundance) and the goal is molecular traits, class assignment, diversity indices, dissimilarity matrices, or region/temperature comparisons of DOM composition.

name: functional-diversity-raoq-cwm-estimation
description: Use when you have an FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table (molecules x samples with relative abundances) plus assigned molecular traits, and need a functional diversity index per sample to test trait-based responses (e.g., to warming).

name: gain-loss-rescoring-visualization
description: Use when comparing PSM identifications across rescoring conditions (e.g. MaxQuant-only, Andromeda+Percolator, Andromeda+Prosit+Percolator) and you need to report gained/lost PSM counts and a gain/loss plot per allele or condition.

name: gan-architecture-implementation
description: Use when a task requires reconstructing or coding a 3D conditional GAN (generator, discriminator, self-attention blocks, spectral normalization) and its composite loss from an architecture description, e.g., MRI/PET synthesis.

name: gan-based-medical-image-synthesis
description: Use when the task is cross-domain neuroimage synthesis (e.g., T1w/FLAIR MRI to PET or DTI-derived maps) or multidimensional diffusion MRI superresolution where stable GAN training and 3D spatial consistency matter.

name: gan-component-ablation-experiment-design
description: Use when a GAN-based synthesis model must be decomposed into architectural/loss components and each component's contribution to image-quality metrics needs to be ranked via controlled ablation.

name: gan-hyperparameter-tuning-cross-validation
description: Use when training conditional GANs (SC-GAN, 2D/3D cGAN, Att cGAN) on 256x256x256 medical images and you need to select hyperparameters (mu, lambda, lr, batch size) fairly via cross-validation before benchmarking.

name: gan-training-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when synthesizing a target modality (PET, FA, or MD maps) from input modalities such as T1w and FLAIR, and you need to train a 3D conditional GAN with tuned regularization, loss weights, and learning-rate settings.

name: gan-training-time-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking training wall-clock cost of GAN models for multimodal neuroimaging synthesis (e.g., T1w+FLAIR to PET/FA/MD tasks) and you need minutes-per-epoch and time-to-plateau per architecture.

name: genome-browser-track-annotation
description: Use when PhosBoost per-site prediction tsv files and DIAMOND inferred-positives csv files exist for a proteome and a genomic gff3 is available, and you need a JBrowse-compatible phosphosite track.

name: genome-wide-phosphoproteome-scoring
description: Use when you have a complete proteome FASTA (e.g. wheat, oat, barley, maize) and pre-trained PhosBoost models, and need phosphorylation probability scores for all S/T/Y residues plus browser visualization tracks.

name: genomic-coordinate-mapping
description: Use when predicted phosphosites given in protein residue coordinates must be projected onto genome coordinates and merged with DIAMOND inferred positives into a GFF3 genome-browser track.

name: geodesic-icosahedron-tessellation
description: Use when you have atomic coordinates of a protein (e.g. a PDB entry such as 1MBN) and need per-residue static solvent accessibility validated against published Lee and Richards values.

name: gff3-annotation-merging
description: Use when PhosBoost prediction TSVs and DIAMOND inferred-positive CSVs must be projected from protein coordinates onto a genomic GFF3 to build a JBrowse visualization track.

name: gpcr-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when building or reproducing a GPCR classification benchmark from UniProt FASTA sequences and you must control sequence homology (CD-Hit identity threshold 0.8) before feature extraction or cross-validation.

name: gpcr-sequence-classification
description: Use when the input is GPCR amino-acid sequences (e.g., a FASTA file) that must be classified as GPCR vs. non-GPCR, or when benchmarking feature representations (BOW, CBOW word-embedding, or their concatenation) for GPCR identification.

name: gpu-compute-cost-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing wall-clock training cost (minutes per epoch, minutes to plateau, GPU memory burden) of a new GAN or network against baseline models on a fixed GPU cluster.

name: gradient-boosting-classification
description: Use when protein sequences have been embedded into high-dimensional deep representation learning vectors (BiLSTM 3605D, UniRep 1900D, TAPE-BERT 768D) and a binary R protein / non-R protein classifier with feature selection is required.

name: gradient-boosting-classifier-training
description: Use when you need to train binary phosphorylation-site classifiers from protein language model embeddings, prioritizing recall with a balanced/equal-weight stacking design.

name: gradient-boosting-feature-ranking
description: Use when a high-dimensional fused protein-embedding feature vector (e.g., 5505D BiLSTM+UniRep) must be ranked and reduced by feature importance before training classifiers such as SVM, LGBM, RF, or ET.

name: gradient-moment-nulling-constraint-design
description: Use when generating time-optimal diffusion gradient waveforms that must suppress motion-induced phase errors (gradient moment compensation up to M2) or eddy-current effects (λ = 40, 80 ms), and when benchmarking on-the-fly generation speed vs. gradient raster time dt.

name: gradient-moment-residual-tolerance-sweep
description: Decision support for choosing motion-compensation convergence tolerances in optimized diffusion gradient waveforms when you need to know which residual M0/M1/M2 magnitudes keep ADC bias within an acceptable bound (e.g., ≤5%).

name: gradient-waveform-comparison-visualization
description: Use when a gradient design task must contrast waveforms solved at derated logical-axis limits against waveforms solved at full hardware limits in the physical coordinate system for an oblique slice orientation.

name: gradient-waveform-time-optimal-optimization
description: Use when a pulse sequence needs the shortest feasible gradient waveform under hardware limits (gmax, smax, raster time dt) plus encoding constraints such as diffusion b-value targets or gradient moment nulling orders.

name: graph-network-construction-and-visualization
description: Use when a human phosphoproteomics differential site regulation table (site IDs, kinase-mappable phosphosites, regulation/differential values) must be turned into a kinase-substrate signaling network that can be visualized and exported.

name: grouped-summary-statistics-computation
description: Use when a continuous omics value (e.g., mRNA expression) for one gene must be summarized per cancer type across a cell line panel (e.g., DepMap, 1773 lines, 34 cancer types) and ranked to identify the highest-expressing groups.

name: half-maximal-fluorescence-tm-calculation
description: Use when 96-well DSF fluorescence-versus-temperature melting curves need Tm determination by the half-maximal-defluorescence (HMD) method, especially to benchmark HMD against FD-derived Tm values and flag two-species or high-background failure cases.

name: heparin-protein-thermal-shift-interpretation
description: Decision support for choosing between HMD and FD Tm determination when analyzing 96-well DSF melting curves — especially heparin-binding thermal shift data where curves may contain two protein species of different Tm values or high initial fluorescence.

name: histone-binary-ptm-abundance-statistics
description: Use when comparing relative abundances of binary (two-mark) histone peptides between conditions (e.g., wt vs Suz12-/- ESCs) across two histone preparations, to identify significantly changed marks with a t-test.

name: histone-combinatorial-ptm-abundance-normalization
description: Use when MS/MS spectra of hypermodified histone tails have been identified by Mascot (e.g. middle-down or top-down analyses with scrambled combinatorial PTMs) and you need relative abundance per combinatorial mark.

name: histone-peptide-ion-intensity-quantification
description: Use when you need relative abundances of hypermodified histone-tail peptides (middle-down/top-down data) from Mascot .csv results, especially where isobaric peptides with different PTM localizations co-fragment and must be deconvoluted.

name: histone-ptm-co-occurrence-frequency-analysis
description: Use when middle-down histone MS/MS data (Mascot .csv + Histone Coder Brno-nomenclature PTM strings) must be tested for co-existence or mutual exclusivity of specific mark pairs, e.g. H3K9me3K27me3 vs H3K18acK23ac.

name: histone-ptm-relative-quantification
description: Use when Mascot .csv search output and a Histone Coder result file are available for histone middle-down ETD spectra and relative abundances of single or combinatorial PTM peptide groups (e.g. 0-3 acetyl, 0-9 methyl) must be quantified across replicates.

name: histone-tail-lc-separation-qc
description: Use when replicate RP/WCX-HILIC LC-MS/MS runs of histone tails are available and run-to-run retention-time stability of H3, H4, and H2A N-terminal tail peaks must be checked against fixed minute-thresholds before PTM quantification.

name: hla-allele-best-score-assignment
description: Use when evaluating predicted MHC-binder fractions for peptide lists from HLA samples with multiple HLA alleles (need -score-across-alleles assignment) or a mono-allelic line with one fixed allele, before applying a percentile-rank binder cutoff.

name: hmm-profile-alignment-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking a plant R protein predictor against the HMMER profile alignment baseline, especially when negative training set sequences are annotated incompletely under HMMER so scoring must be restricted to positive sequences.

name: hydrogen-bond-pattern-recognition
description: Use when per-residue secondary structure assignments (helices, ladders, sheets, turns, bends) must be derived from backbone hydrogen-bond patterns in an mmCIF/PDB structure using DSSP.

name: icer-index-computation
description: Use when you have a DOM molecular compositional matrix (FT-ICR MS) plus per-sample environmental metadata (e.g., temperature) and need a sample-level indicator of compositional-level environmental response, such as DOM thermal response to experimental warming.

name: image-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when 3D medical image synthesis outputs (e.g., 256x256x256 PET volumes from T1w/FLAIR MRI) must be scored against ground-truth volumes to compare competing networks (SC-GAN vs 2D/3D cGAN, Att cGAN).

name: imbalanced-class-weight-configuration
description: Use when training a peptide/site classifier on imbalanced positive:negative data (e.g., few SNO sites vs many non-SNO sites) and you need loss re-weighting before softmax output rather than resampling.

name: imbalanced-label-evaluation-metrics
description: Use when benchmarking binary classifiers on sparsely labeled positives (e.g., Ser/Thr/Tyr phosphosites from qPTMplants) where accuracy and AUROC alone are mis and per-class recall/AUPRC tradeoffs must be reported.

name: immunopeptidomics-fdr-filtering
description: Use when PSM or peptide results from immunopeptidomics database searches (MS-GF+, Comet, X!Tandem, MaxQuant) must be filtered at a controlled false discovery rate before downstream rescoring, RT model training, or peptide-count comparisons.

name: immunopeptidomics-peptide-validation-tabulation
description: Use when a paper reports a subset of MHC-binding or neoantigen peptide identifications selected for synthetic peptide validation and you must independently confirm detection status by searching a synthetic-peptide-only database and comparing to the reported outcome.

name: immunopeptidomics-psm-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw immunopeptidomics MGF files and search engine outputs (e.g., Comet .pep.xml against A1101-style data) must be rescored with deep learning features to increase MHC-binding peptide identification sensitivity.

name: independent-test-set-evaluation
description: Use when a trained plant R protein predictor must be fairly benchmarked against prior predictors (prPred, HMMER) on a held-out, non-redundant independent test set rather than on cross-validation alone.

name: independent-test-set-evaluation
description: Use when a trained S-nitrosylation site predictor must be scored on a held-out independent test set (Xie et al. benchmark, CD-HIT 40%) with Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC and benchmarked against baseline predictors.

name: information-entropy-calculation-per-position
description: Use when a multiple sequence alignment of protein variants exists (or can be built with MUSCLE) and per-position conservation diversity must be quantified as information entropy and mapped onto a 3D structure via B-values.

name: intra-protein-cv-precision-analysis
description: Use when comparing SPS-MS3 or RTS-MS3 isobaric peptide quantification precision: you have IsobaricQuant score tables (isopep_extra.csv) and want to know whether QC-score filtering reduces intra-protein CVs without depleting protein coverage.

name: intravoxel-phase-dispersion-simulation
description: Decision support for choosing allowable residual moment tolerances (M0/M1/M2) in motion-compensated diffusion gradient design, when you must trade optimizer compute time against ADC accuracy ≤5%.

name: ion-image-slice-extraction
description: Use when an MS imaging dataset (one MassSpectrum object per tissue pixel) must be summarized into a mean spectrum and rendered as spatial ion-image slices at selected m/z values, e.g. reproducing the mouse kidney MALDI imaging Figure 7 layout.

name: irt-to-retention-time-alignment
description: Use when building rescoring features for PSM-level FDR estimation: you have search engine results with confident target PSMs, Prosit-predicted iRT values, and need a ΔRT (predicted vs. observed RT) feature column for mokapot/percolator rescoring.

name: isobaric-peptide-abundance-deconvolution
description: Use when middle-down (or top-down) histone MS/MS data contain co-fragmenting isobaric polypeptide species sharing the same sequence but different PTM localizations (e.g. H3K18ac vs H3K23ac), and per-localization relative abundances are needed for PTM cross-talk analysis.

name: isobaric-peptide-cofragmentation-splitting
description: Use when MS/MS spectra of histone tails (middle-down/top-down) contain co-eluting isobaric peptides that share the same sequence but differ in PTM localization, and each species must be apportioned a share of the composite spectrum's total ion intensity.

name: isobaric-peptide-fragment-ion-ratio-correction
description: Use when middle-down or top-down histone MS/MS data contain isobaric polypeptide species that co-fragment — i.e., identical peptide sequences with distinct PTM localizations (e.g., K4me3 vs K14ac positional isomers) — and relative abundances per localization are needed.

name: isobaric-peptide-fragment-ratio-quantification
description: Use when quantifying co-isolated, co-fragmented isobaric histone peptide forms (same sequence, distinct PTM localizations) from middle-down or top-down ETD MS/MS spectra, where XIC or spectral counting is inadequate.

name: isobaric-peptide-qc-score-filtering
description: Use when TMT/iTRAQ PSM quantification tables are impaired by precursor co-isolation (ratio compression) and you need to remove inaccurate peptide quantifications at MS2 or MS3 level before protein-level aggregation.

name: isobaric-quantification-cross-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when validating that a new or custom reporter-ion quantification tool produces intensities consistent with established software (FragPipe, MaxQuant) on isobarically-labeled TMT/TMTpro data acquired at MS2 or MS3 level.

name: isobaric-reporter-ion-quantification
description: Use when quantifying TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ reporter ions from mzML spectra plus PSM hits, or when filtering isobarically-labeled scans suffering precursor interference/compression prior to protein-level quantification.

name: isobaric-tmt-peptide-quantification
description: Use when quantifying TMT, TMTpro, or iTRAQ reporter ions from mzML files with a search-engine PSM table, especially when co-isolation interference may distort ratios and scan-level filtering is desired.

name: isoform-proteoform-abundance-estimation
description: Use when peptide-spectrum matches from Morpheus contain peptides shared across multiple proteins, and abundance estimates are needed for protein families or isoforms/proteoforms rather than only individually resolved proteins.

name: isotopic-envelope-visualization
description: Use when you have a raw MS run (e.g. PXD000001, TMT experiment from a Thermo Orbitrap Q Exactive) and need scan-level visual exploration: heat maps, 3D scan maps, or isotopic-envelope zooms, in R.

name: itraq-4plex-ms2-spectrum-overlay-visualization
description: Use when raw MS2 spectra of one identified peptide exist at multiple precursor charge states (e.g. iTRAQ 4-plex) and the goal is an overlaid, fragment-annotated comparison plot in R.

name: java-interface-implementation
description: Use when building Java software that must read several MS peak list formats (e.g. for mzIdentML consumers) and you want one parser interface (lookup by index, ID, scan number) instead of per-format code paths.

name: java-library-benchmarking
description: Use when you must measure how fast and how memory-light a Java parser runs on XML result files of increasing size — e.g. X!Tandem output files with 3225, 60902, or 233327 quality spectra — against a published reference.

name: java-mass-spectrometry-parser-reconstruction
description: Use when a text-format peak list file (e.g. MGF with BEGIN IONS/END IONS blocks) must be converted into structured spectrum records with per-spectrum parameters and peak lists in a memory-efficient streaming design.

name: java-parser-api-integration
description: Use when a Java workflow must read MS peak list or XML-based MS data (mzXML, mzML, mzData, MGF, DTA, MS2, PKL, PRIDE XML) and spectra referenced by mzIdentML need uniform programmatic access.

name: kinase-activity-aggregation-scoring
description: Use when a differential human phosphoproteomics site table (site IDs, regulation/differential values) must be transformed into kinase-level activity scores and a kinase-substrate signaling network, rather than remaining at single-site resolution.

name: koina-prediction-server-querying
description: Use when peptides (from a .csv precursor list or in-silico-digested FASTA) need predicted fragment intensities or iRT values to build a Spectronaut-compatible .csv/.msp spectral library or generate rescoring features.

name: lc-ms-raw-data-import
description: Use when a raw MS run (e.g. an mzML/TMT experiment such as PXD000001 acquired on a Thermo Orbitrap Q Exactive) must be loaded into R at scan level to plot retention-time vs m/z heat maps, 3D scan maps, or MS/MS2 spectra.

name: lc-msms-biomarker-list-filtering
description: Use when MALDI imaging proteolytic peaks (m/z [M+H]+ list) need to be annotated against LC-MS/MS proteomic discovery data, and a gene-name cluster list must first be used to restrict candidate biomarkers before correlation matching.

name: lcms-peptide-mass-table-parsing
description: Use when a MALDI-to-LC-MS matching step needs a reference table of LC-MS/MS peptide masses (e.g., peptides.txt) and the table must be read and formatted in R before tolerance-based mass correlation.

name: lgbm-feature-selection-and-classification
description: Use when you have a high-dimensional fused protein embedding (e.g., 5505D BiLSTM+UniRep vectors from FASTA sequences) and need feature selection plus a strong classifier for binary protein-family prediction with accuracy/F1/AUC evaluation.

name: local-window-deviation-calculation
description: Use when you have an X-ray protein structure in PDB format and need to detect residues whose mobility (Cα B-factor) deviates from their local sequence neighborhood, e.g. for protein-ligand interaction analysis.

name: log10-reporter-intensity-correlation-analysis
description: Use when validating that a new reporter-ion quantification tool produces intensities consistent with tools, by reprocessing the same mzML files with multiple tools and correlating their log10 reporter intensities on shared scan groups.

name: lowess-curve-fitting
description: Use when search-engine PSMs need a retention-time-based rescoring feature: Prosit iRT predictions for confident target PSMs must be mapped through a LOWESS fit to observed RT so ΔRT deviations can separate correct from incorrect PSMs.

name: ma-plot-construction
description: Use when the goal is to visualize log2 reporter-intensity ratios between two TMT channels (e.g. TMT129 or TMT131 vs TMT127) as MA scatter plots, especially to contrast R's base, lattice and ggplot2 plotting systems on the same data.

name: magnetic-resonance-fingerprinting-dictionary-matching
description: Use when quantitative CEST parameter maps (fMT, kMT, fAmide, kAmide) must be derived from spin-lock-based CEST-MRF acquisitions, especially for cross-site or multi-scanner reproducibility studies.

name: magnetization-transfer-pool-modeling
description: Use when the goal is to simulate, compare, or optimize CEST pre-saturation protocols defined as Pulseq .seq-files — e.g., predicting the Z-spectrum of an APTw preparation block before scanner time, or checking that a shared protocol behaves as expected.

name: maldi-imaging-peptide-annotation
description: Use when a mass-matched peptide identification table (e.g. MaxQuant-style 'peptides.txt') must be filtered to peptides whose 'Gene names' field overlaps a differential-abundance signature list (e.g. proteins enriched in an HSIL(+) tissue cluster) before MALDI peak annotation.

name: maldi-imaging-spectrum-averaging
description: Use when the input is an MS imaging acquisition (a mass spectrum per pixel across a tissue section, e.g. the mouse kidney MALDI imaging demonstration dataset) and the goal is to summarize it as a mean spectrum plus spatial ion-image slices around its highest peaks in R.

name: maldi-mz-to-neutral-mass-conversion
description: Use when you have MALDI imaging peak lists of monoisotopic [M+H]+ m/z values (positive mode) and an LC-MS/MS peptide mass table (peptides.txt), and need to identify which MALDI peaks correspond to proteolytic peptides.

name: maldi-peak-protein-correlation
description: Use when proteolytic peaks from bottom-up MALDI imaging must be assigned more specific protein identities by correlating MALDI m/z [M+H]+ peaks with LC-MS/MS biomarker discovery data restricted to a gene-name list of interest.

name: maldi-tof-spectrum-preprocessing
description: Use when a single MALDI-TOF (2D MS1-level) spectrum must be transformed, smoothed, baseline-corrected and peak-picked, and each preprocessing step needs to be visually inspected before downstream analysis.

name: mascot-output-parsing
description: Use when raw Mascot search results from middle-down histone LC-MS/MS (ETD/CID-HCD) runs must be converted to Histone Coder/isoScale inputs, or when PTM-localized peptide-spectrum matches in Brno nomenclature (e.g. K4me3K14ac) are needed downstream.

name: mascot-result-parsing
description: Use when Mascot database-search results (in .xml for PTM-localization validation or .csv for peptide quantification) must be parsed, filtered, and converted into Brno nomenclature combinatorial histone marks.

name: mascot-search-output-parsing
description: Use when ingesting Mascot Server output (peptide identifications, iTRAQ reporter-ion quantitation, or Mascot Distiller quantitation) into a peptide-centric relational store linked to source mass spectra.

name: mass-difference-edge-annotation
description: Use when a raw MS/MS peak list must be transformed into a de novo-style spectrum graph whose nodes carry mass/intensity and edges carry mass differences, as required before Popitam-style graph parsing.

name: mass-peak-picking-and-intensity-ranking
description: Use when a mass spectrometry imaging dataset contains one MassSpectrum per pixel and you need a summarized mean spectrum plus spatial ion-image slices centered on the most intense peaks.

name: mass-spectrometry-charge-state-handling
description: Use when you have a list of monoisotopic [M+H]+ m/z peaks from positive-mode MALDI imaging and an LC-MS/MS peptide mass table (e.g., peptides.txt) and must correlate peaks to identified peptides by mass.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-management
description: Use when raw vendor-specific MS/MS peak lists must be converted to Mascot Generic File (MGF) format, persisted in a central proteomics database, and later interrogated via filtered peptide/protein lists and descriptive statistics.

name: mass-spectrometry-data-processing
description: Use when a mass-matched peptide identification table must be restricted to proteins from a differential-abundance signature list before annotating MALDI imaging peaks with LC-MS/MS-derived identifications.

name: mass-spectrometry-record-serialization
description: Use when input is a peak list or XML-based MS data file (DTA, MS2, MGF, PKL, mzXML, mzData, mzML, PRIDE XML) referenced by mzIdentML, and the goal is extracting per-spectrum records (id, CV parameters, peak lists) into structured JSON.

name: mass-spectrometry-spectrum-archival-schema-design
description: Use when a laboratory needs a central relational database schema to store, link, and archive mass spectra, peptide identifications, and quantitative results from MS-driven proteomics experiments.

name: maxquant-peptide-table-parsing
description: Use when a MaxQuant-exported peptides.txt table must be loaded into R and paired with a MALDI m/z [M+H]+ peak list and a gene-name list to identify MALDI imaging proteolytic peaks.
