description: Use when you have a FASTA file of protein sequence variants (or a UniprotID) and need to quantify per-position conservation/entropy and visualize it on a 3D protein structure from the PDB.

name: sequence-homology-reduction
description: Use when building a protein benchmark dataset from raw database downloads (e.g. UniProt FASTA) where redundant homologous sequences must be removed before training or cross-validating a classifier such as EMCBOW-GPCR.

name: sequence-identity-thresholding
description: Use when a labeled protein sequence dataset (e.g., positive/negative FASTA files of plant R proteins) must be deduplicated before feature extraction and model construction to remove redundant homologs.

name: sequence-position-to-structure-residue-mapping
description: Use when per-position sequence conservation, entropy, or SNP frequency/type values from a multiple sequence alignment must be visualized on a protein 3D structure by rewriting PDB B-value columns.

name: signal-smoothing-window-selection
description: Use when a normalized melting curve from DSF analysis needs smoothing before Tm analysis and noise reduction must not distort the pre- and post-denaturation baseline shape.

name: silhouette-based-wordbook-size-selection
description: Use when converting GPCR (or other protein) sequences into bag-of-words features and the number of words in the wordbook must be determined from the data via the weighted Silhouette Coefficient.

name: simulation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or validating the computational performance of a CEST Bloch-McConnell simulation (e.g. pulseq-cest-sim) against published per-Z-spectrum runtime benchmarks.

name: single-peak-detection-from-mass-spectra
description: Use when working with raw MALDI-TOF or other 2D MS1-level spectra in R and you need to inspect every preprocessing step (transformation, smoothing, baseline correction, peak picking) in detail.

name: site-determining-ion-counting
description: Use when Mascot (.xml) results from ETD middle-down analysis of hypermodified histone tails must have PTM sites unambiguously localized before downstream quantification (isoScale) or mark counting.

name: slice-obliquity-hardware-derating
description: Use when designing GrOpt gradient waveforms targeting an oblique slice and you must decide between derating Gmax/Smax by a rotation factor versus rotating constraints into the physical gradient coordinate system for the specific slice orientation.

name: smote-class-imbalance-handling
description: Use when the GPCR benchmark dataset is class-imbalanced and you must compare classifiers under the SMOTE 300% positive-sample balancing protocol with 5-fold cross-validation, e.g. reproducing the EMCBOW-GPCR vs. Liao baseline Table 3 comparison.

name: sno-site-onehot-sequence-encoding
description: Use when preparing peptide windows around candidate SNO sites for a deep-learning classifier (e.g. SNO-DCA) and the input is raw protein sequences, not a precomputed feature table.

name: sno-site-prediction-model-ablation
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that individual deep-learning components (dense convolutional blocks, channel attention) measurably improve site-prediction performance over a plain CNN baseline, using ten-fold cross-validation on sliding-window peptide fragments.

name: spatial-proteomics-pca-ordination
description: Use when a quantitative spatial proteomics dataset (e.g. an MSnSet such as tan2009r1 from pRolocdata) needs 2D ordination for visualising subcellular niches and per-protein SVM classification confidence.

name: spectral-angle-similarity-scoring
description: Use when rescoring PSMs from immunopeptidomics database searches (Comet, MS-GF+, X!Tandem, MaxQuant) and you want to quantify how well a deep learning spectrum prediction (pDeep2) matches the observed MS/MS spectrum as a discriminative feature.

name: spectral-count-protein-quantification
description: Use when raw LC-MS/MS data have been searched with the Morpheus peptide-MS/MS matching engine and per-protein relative abundances must be quantified label-free from spectral counts, especially across protein families or isoforms.

name: spectral-counting-quantification
description: Use when quantifying histone PTM peptide groups label-free from Mascot database-search results, or when benchmarking spectral counting against MS/MS ion-intensity (isoScale) and XIC quantification across technical replicates.

name: spectral-intensity-transformation
description: Use when you need to preprocess and inspect a single MALDI-TOF or other 2D MS1-level mass spectrum in R, starting with intensity transformation to stabilize variance across the mass range before smoothing, baseline removal, and peak detection.

name: spectral-library-format-generation
description: Use when a DIA/search workflow requires a predicted spectral library and the input is either a .csv of precursor peptides or a proteome .fasta needing in silico digestion into target-decoy libraries.

name: spectral-normalization-implementation
description: Use when building or reproducing a GAN (e.g., 3D conditional GAN for MRI/PET synthesis) whose training is unstable, and you need weight normalization in generator and discriminator layers as done in SC-GAN.

name: spectral-peak-annotation-of-psms
description: Use when MaxQuant (or another search engine) PSM results plus raw/mzML spectra must be annotated with predicted fragment intensities to build features for data-driven rescoring with mokapot or percolator.

name: spectral-peak-annotation-with-predicted-fragments
description: Use when annotating experimental peaks of search-engine PSMs (e.g. MaxQuant/Andromeda results converted via pp.convert_search/pp.load_search) with Prosit fragment intensity and iRT predictions from Koina to generate rescoring features.

name: spectral-peak-list-conversion
description: Use when heterogeneous vendor-specific MS/MS peak list files must be normalized to MGF and ingested into the central ms_lims database for MS-driven proteomics data management.

name: spectral-peak-pair-parsing
description: Use when input is a text-format peak list file such as MGF (with BEGIN IONS / END IONS blocks, TITLE/PEPMASS/CHARGE/RTINSECONDS headers and peak lines) and you need structured spectrum records with peak pairs for downstream search or QC.

name: spectral-prediction-feature-generation
description: Use when rescoring PSMs from immunopeptidomics (HLA-bound peptide) database searches, where unspecific cleavage inflates the search space and adding RT- and spectrum-prediction features can raise sensitivity and confidence of MHC-binding peptide and neoantigen identifications.

name: spectral-smoothing-and-baseline-correction
description: Use when a raw MALDI-TOF (or other 2D MS1-level) mass spectrum loaded in R must be cleaned for peak picking, and each preprocessing stage (transformed, smoothed, baseline-corrected, peak-picked) needs to be visually inspectable.

name: spectrum-graph-construction
description: Use when raw MS/MS peak lists must be converted into a de novo-style spectrum graph (nodes = peaks with mass/intensity, edges = mass differences) as the input representation for peptide identification by matching against a sequence database.

name: spectrum-graph-path-scoring
description: Use when characterizing peptides with mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications from MS/MS data by searching a peptide sequence database, especially with low-quality spectra or large databases.

name: spectrum-header-field-extraction
description: Use when input is an MS2 (or other peak list) file from a proteomics workflow and each spectrum's charge state, precursor m/z, retention time, and peak list must be extracted into structured records, e.g. for mzIdentML-referenced spectra.

name: spectrum-peak-array-extraction
description: Use when an mzML (or another jmzReader-supported peak list/XML format such as mzXML, MGF, PRIDE XML) file must be read in a Java project to obtain per-spectrum MS level, precursor ion information, and peak m/z/intensity lists.

name: spectrum-record-schema-construction
description: Use when input is a PKL (or similar plain-text peak list: DTA, MS2, MGF) mass spectrometry file and spectra must be converted into structured records with precursor metadata plus peak lists.

name: spreadsheet-data-import
description: Use when the input is a single .xlsx, .csv or .txt file containing at least a Concentration column and a Measurement column from a targeted MS (SRM/MRM/PRM) dilution series, and the goal is to prepare data for calibration-curve fitting with CalibraCurve.

name: sps-ms3-interference-assessment
description: Use when TMT/TMTpro iTRAQ data acquired with SPS-MS3 or RTS-MS3 shows ratio compression from co-isolated co-eluting precursors, and you need to filter interfered peptide quantifications (isopep_extra.csv score tables) prior to protein-level quantification.

name: sps-ms3-qc-score-filtering
description: Use when quantifying TMT/iTRAQ-labeled peptides with IsobaricQuant (MS2 or SPS-MS3 mzML) and co-isolation interference must be filtered by QC scores before protein-level aggregation or differential testing.

name: stacking-ensemble-model-training
description: Use when a labeled, class-imbalanced biosequence dataset has per-residue feature embeddings (e.g., ProtT5 residue plus protein-average vectors) and a stacked binary classifier must be built and compared against its base classifiers.

name: stratified-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when a user-defined multiomics signature (e.g. the 15-gene hypoxia signature) must be tested for its ability to predict a user-defined drug response (e.g. Nilotinib) from GDSC cell-line data with an AUC-quantified ML evaluation.

name: structure-based-drug-design
description: Use when a protein X-ray structure is available and you want to derive a pharmacophore model whose features are annotated with B'-factor/ΔB' support from BANΔIT to guide inhibitor design.

name: structure-based-drug-design-b-factor-annotation
description: Use when X-ray crystal structures of protein-ligand complexes (with raw B-factors) are available and you need to assess ligand-induced rigidification or flexibility gain at the binding site for drug optimization decisions.

name: subsample-resampling-omics
description: Use when you need to identify which omic features (e.g. proteomics variables) are stably predictive across a dataset, rather than trusting a single model fit, and you want signatures with similar predictive performance.

name: surface-plot-visualization-of-curve-differences
description: Use when raw and smoothed melting curves (e.g. from SimpleDSFviewer's built-in MC smoothing in Matlab) must be compared point-wise to quantify and display how much smoothing distorts the MC surface.

name: svm-confidence-point-size-encoding
description: Use when visualizing a spatial proteomics MSnSet on a PCA ordination and you need to communicate classifier confidence alongside organelle assignments, e.g. after pRoloc SVM classification with per-feature scores.

name: synthetic-peptide-lc-msms-confirmation
description: Use when a shortlist of candidate MHC-binding or neoantigen peptides (e.g. selected at q-value <= 0.01 from a DeepRescore result) needs experimental confirmation against synthetic peptide standards, or when verifying that rescued peptide IDs correspond to real analytes.

name: tab-delimited-proteomics-report-export
description: Use when you have an X!Tandem output XML file and need each identification's peptide sequence, E-value, hyperscore, protein accession, and spectrum details (charge, precursor and fragment m/z) dumped as a flat table.

name: tabular-column-annotation-r
description: Use when a MaxQuant peptides.txt (or similar peptide-by-replicate intensity matrix) must be annotated with per-condition aggregate columns such as 'Average Intensity_<condition>' and '#Positive Replicates_<condition>'.

name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-peptide-identification
description: Use when MS/MS spectra must be identified against a peptide sequence database, especially when mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications may be present or spectra are of low quality.

name: tandem-mass-spectrometry-spectrum-representation
description: Use when you need to convert raw tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) peak lists into a de novo-style spectrum graph that a sequence-database search or ACO-based parser can traverse, especially for peptides with mutations or unexpected PTMs.

name: tandem-ms-result-parsing
description: Use when the input is an X!Tandem XML output file from a tandem MS search and you need to extract peptide sequences, E-values, hyperscores, modifications, or fragment-ion m/z and intensity values programmatically.

name: target-decoy-fdr-estimation
description: Use when annotated PSMs have been rescored with Prosit/Koina-derived features (e.g. spectral angle, intensity features, merged MaxQuant scores) and confidently identified peptides/PSMs must be counted at 1% FDR via target/decoy competition.

name: target-decoy-fdr-filtering
description: Use when peptide identifications from search engines (Comet, MS-GF+, X!Tandem, MaxQuant) must be filtered to 1% FDR at PSM and peptide levels before overlap, ablation, or neoantigen analyses.

name: targeted-proteomics-assay-validation
description: Use when a dilution/concentration series of replicate measurements (e.g., transition-level intensities from an Agilent 6490 MRM run or msqc1 data) must be converted into a validated calibration curve with a defensible linear range and quantification limits.

name: targeted-proteomics-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when concentration/dilution-series data from targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM, e.g., msqc1 heavy/light peptide peak areas) must be converted into calibration curves with LLOQ/ULOQ and linear-range estimates, or compared across instruments.

name: targeted-proteomics-dilution-series-analysis
description: Use when a replicate intensity table from a concentration or dilution series (e.g. msqc1 calibration data) must be reduced to a linear quantification range via per-level replicate CV against a threshold TMeasCV.

name: targeted-proteomics-linear-range-output
description: Use when targeted MS (SRM/MRM or PRM) calibration data from concentration or dilution series with known analyte amounts must yield an automated linear range (LLOQ/ULOQ) and fitted calibration curves for downstream concentration prediction.

name: temperature-gradient-trend-regression
description: Use when a FT-ICR MS molecular compositional table sampled across multiple temperature levels (e.g., six levels in temperate and subtropical regions) must be tested for significant diversity-temperature trends.

name: tensorflow-gpu-distributed-training
description: Use when training a 3D conditional GAN (e.g., SC-GAN) in TensorFlow on 256x256x256 multimodal MRI volumes to synthesize PET, FA, or MD maps, or when GPU memory constraints force batch size 1 and stabilized training (spectral normalization, feature matching) is needed.

name: tensorflow-model-instantiation-verification
description: Use when a paper's neural architecture (e.g. SC-GAN: 3D cGAN + self-attention + spectral normalization) has been reimplemented and you must verify the model graph constructs correctly and matches a reference implementation.

name: theoretical-fragment-ion-matching
description: Use when candidate theoretical peptides from a sequence database must be scored against an MS/MS spectrum — especially for peptides carrying mutations or unexpected post-translational modifications.

name: theoretical-peptide-sequence-matching
description: Use when identifying peptides from tandem mass spectrometry (MS/MS) data by database search, especially when mutations or unexpected PTMs are expected or the spectrum is of low quality.

name: thermal-denaturation-curve-classification
description: Use when automating DSF Tm screening over many melting curves and needing rules to accept secondary Tms, reject noisy peaks, flag uninterpretable curves, or detect pre-denatured samples.

name: thermal-proteome-profiling-analysis
description: Use when reprocessing TMTpro isobaric-labeled PISA/thermal-proteome raw data (e.g., PRIDE PXD014369) to compare unfiltered vs. QC-filtered protein quantification and count significant thermal-shift drug targets.

name: tmt-interference-qc-score-filtering
description: Use when isobarically-labeled (TMT/TMTpro/iTRAQ) MS2 or RTS-MS3 reporter-ion quantifications suffer precursor interference (ratio compression) and you want to filter inaccurate scans with QC score cutoffs before protein-level quantification.

name: tmt-reporter-channel-ratio-analysis
description: Use when you have TMT reporter-ion intensities from a labelled MS experiment and need per-feature log2 channel ratios (M) versus mean log2 intensity (A) plotted as MA plots, e.g. to visualise ratio spread between reporter channels.

name: training-convergence-plateau-detection
description: Use when comparing the training wall-clock cost of generative models (minutes per epoch, time to plateau) or when you must document the computational burden of a 3D GAN before committing GPU resources.

name: transcript-protein-count-verification
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a curated gene family database and you must confirm that homolog, transcript, and protein counts match published totals before downstream structural or phylogenetic analyses.

name: uloq-out-of-range-prediction-flagging
description: Use when new intensity values from an SRM/MRM or PRM targeted MS assay (e.g. msqc1 dilution-series data) must be converted to concentrations with a fitted CalibraCurve model, and out-of-linear-range values must be flagged.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you need a 2D visual check that a selected feature subset (e.g., LGBM-ranked features from fused BiLSTM 3605D + UniRep 1900D embeddings) separates two protein classes before or after classifier training.

name: vendor-sequence-framework-integration
description: Use when you need to play out a vendor-independent CEST preparation block defined in a Pulseq .seq file on a scanner while preserving an existing native readout sequence, its UI, and its reconstruction unchanged.

name: wallclock-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing the Figure 4 runtime scaling evaluation: six HLA search-result datasets of varying PSM counts need per-step (conversion, prediction, rescoring) and total wall-clock timings to test linear scaling with PSM count.

name: warming-response-network-comparison
description: Use when paired DOM molecular intensity (FT-ICR MS) and microbial abundance tables are available under warming vs control treatments in multiple regions, and the goal is testing whether bipartite network specialization (H2′) responds to warming.

name: wasabi-b0-field-correction
description: Use when CEST Z-spectral imaging volumes (e.g. APTw pulseq-file acquisitions at 3 T) require B0 inhomogeneity correction before voxel-wise MTRasym(3.5 ppm) extraction, as in healthy-volunteer or tumor-patient in vivo data.

name: weighted-least-squares-calibration-fitting
description: Use when building calibration curves from targeted proteomics dilution series (e.g. Agilent 6490 MRM data in PASSEL) and comparing unweighted vs. weighted (1/x^2) linear fits on the final linear range.

name: white-matter-roi-segmentation-spm
description: Use when you need a tissue-defined region of interest (white matter) to tabulate or compare MTRasym(3.5 ppm) contrast values from processed CEST/Z-spectral data across protocols or subjects.

name: word2vec-cbow-model-training
description: Use when you need to convert protein/GPCR primary sequences into fixed-length word-embedding features by splitting them into l-mers (l=2,3,4), training CBOW models on the resulting wordbooks, and aggregating word vectors per sequence.

name: wt-vs-knockout-ptm-comparison
description: Use when two genotypes (e.g., wt vs a knockout like Suz12-/-) have been quantified for combinatorial histone marks in more than one histone preparation (purified H3 vs crude mixture), and you must test which binary marks change significantly and whether the preparations agree.

name: xtandem-xml-object-model-access
description: Use when the input is an X!Tandem XML output file from tandem MS/MS searching and per-peptide details (sequence, expectation value, hyperscore, modifications, spectra) must be extracted programmatically in Java.

name: xtandem-xml-result-parsing
description: Use when you have X!Tandem XML output files from tandem MS/MS protein identification searches and need to programmatically extract detailed per-spectrum identification information, e.g. into a tab-delimited table.

name: yu-negative-sample-segmentation
description: Use when benchmarking a GPCR-identification predictor against the 400D + PC-PseAAC mixed-feature baseline of Yu et al. under Yu's segmentation strategy, where negatives are divided into 4 groups of 2495 sequences.

name: z-spectrum-normalization-and-mtrasym-calculation
description: Use when you have simulated and/or measured CEST Z-spectra (water z-magnetization vs saturation offset) and need a common normalized scale and asymmetric-contrast (MTRasym) curves before comparing protocols or against scanner data.

name: z-spectrum-simulation
description: Use when a CEST saturation protocol is defined as a Pulseq .seq-file and an in-silico Z-spectrum is needed to test, optimize, or cross-validate the preparation block before or instead of scanner measurement.
